Any bastrop_tx-entitled caller reads all 11 department domains today, including src/mygov-live.mjs:131's unredacted `subject: row.title` on real work-order records (the citizen-name/phone-number carrier the operator's dispatch cites) and the raw row.department field (line 138) that is read off the source system but never consulted by any access check -- worth investigating as a possible data-level anchor for a future department filter, with the caveat that its reliability/coverage as a real department signal is unverified and was out of this lane's authorized scope to probe live.

plan-review's and smart-files' single bastrop_tx persona is mislabeled for its actual current use: 'Development services staff / bastrop_tx' is literally the only identity available to a Fire, Police, Public Works, or Fleet/Finance staffer using either product today. This is a symptom of the G-115 item 5 pilot scope, not a bug in this lane's authorized touch surface, and is named here rather than silently fixed (label-only changes were not this mission's mandate and a mislabel is arguably more honest than a differently-wrong department claim).

The shared-role-model question (CP2) resolves toward 'one source of truth, shape undetermined' -- undetermined specifically because plan-review and smart-files are separate repos/seats with no existing shared-config or shared-identity-service infrastructure, and building that infrastructure's shape is a decision that should follow the operator's ruling on staff authentication below, not precede it.

Two-thirds of the operator's named department list (development-services, public-works, police, fire-ems, fleet) already exists as lensId values inside smartcity-dashboards' own DOMAIN_REGISTRY, with no standalone 'finance' -- consistent with, but not proof of, 'Fleet and Finance' being one combined department rather than two. Handed forward as an observation, explicitly not adopted as the roster (mission instruction: do not infer the roster from the lens list).
missionPremise: G-115 item 5's operator ruling accepted the existing persona-list model as a pilot measure 'scoped to a small named set of invited Bastrop staff,' with real tenancy and auth 'separately tracked, revisited before any wider rollout.' This dispatch's own framing: 'RBAC is what replaces that model, not what supplements it.' This lane's finding is that the prerequisite for that replacement -- a real per-staff-member identity to attach a department claim to -- has not itself been built in any of the three products (source: CP1 surfacesRead, probe P1/P3/P4), so the replacement cannot be built yet without either inventing that identity layer unilaterally (a materially larger, un-scoped piece of work) or getting direction on where it will come from.
completionPredicate: This lane is complete not by shipping a role layer but by handing the operator a scoped, evidence-backed set of blocking questions with a recommended default for each, sufficient to rule on without further investigation: (1) How will Bastrop staff actually authenticate as individuals -- a new build, or an existing mechanism this lane's reads did not surface? (2) What is the real, ratified Bastrop department roster (this lane found none; recommend confirming or replacing the five-plus-finance provisional list surfaced in CP1)? (3) Where should the resulting role model live given plan-review and smart-files already share one persona list and dashboards has none (this lane recommends one shared source of truth in direction, not in concrete shape)? Deny-by-default is NOT included as an open question -- this lane resolved it outright per CP2. A follow-on lane, dispatched after these are ruled on, builds the actual middleware/query-filter/type per the mission's design constraints, which remain valid and unconsumed by this close.
scopeBasis: Read-only across all three named products (smartcity-dashboards, plan-review, smart-files) plus the two governing runbooks; zero code changes, zero PRs, zero deploys -- this lane never reached the build phase because CP2's analysis determined the prerequisite (a ruled department roster and a named staff-identity mechanism) is missing, and the mission's own Close section names exactly this outcome as a valid, preferred one over building on a guess. Cross-tenant isolation (G-126, verified closed above) and the v1 regression (G-122) were out of scope and not touched, matching the dispatch. smartcity-os was read only insofar as G-126's own close already documented it (row.department, dbPermitToApi's shape); no new smartcity-os file was opened and no live request was made against it by this lane.
